title: UI round 3 · S5: type (about four sizes, no phone shrink, mono only for facts)
description:
Slice 5 of 5 of LIN-4040 (UI round 3: Home and the run control). Feedback items 21–23. Lands last, after slice 4, because it touches every surface.

## This piece's slice of the approved plan (D7, type)

**Approach:** use about four font sizes, through the existing token set (LIN-4015, one CSS token set). Body text doesn't shrink on a phone. Mono is only for IDs and figures; the ruling options, "N sessions" and session names are not mono.

**Coordination:** LIN-4017 (Theseus the stylesheet) touches the same stylesheets. Whichever of the two lands first, the other rebases on it. Check its state before you start, and say on both tickets which one is landing first.

## Testing (witness)

* A test that parses the stylesheets Home and the task page load. It fails if there are more than four distinct `font-size` values, if any max-width rule reduces body size for Home classes, or if the ruling options, "N sessions" or session names carry the mono class.
* Screenshots at 390px show body text at the desktop size.

## Done for the parent

After this slice, every item in the feedback doc must be reached, or answered in a PR with a reason, across the five slices. Item 25 (the view bar) stays as it is until John says which views stay. The PR also says that `truncated` workspaces (Jira and GitHub Projects only) leave the held set cold and so get no offer, so readers don't take it for a Linear gap. Post the item-by-item tally on LIN-4040.

Session fit: fits one session

**Grounding commit:** `27ae64ad` (LinearViewer `origin/main`, the sha the plan was written and reviewed against; still HEAD at breakdown, 1 Nov 20:45Z).

**Plan-review due:** no — covered by LIN-4040's approving plan-review (comment `b12f09b0-f5e1-4782-aab9-c38065fbf173`, rev 1 of the fresh 1 Nov plan).

**Starting point:** the parent's approved plan is this piece's starting point. Read it in full in LIN-4040's description (`## Implementation Plan`, decisions D1–D7, "Slices and order", "How it breaks") and the review notes in comment `b12f09b0`. The feedback itself is `docs/reviews/ui-feedback-round-3-2026-10-30/README.md` (25 numbered items with screenshots). Follow the plan; where the code shows it wrong, change course and say so on LIN-4040.

**Every slice:** run the plan's three greps at start and end (each hit is "display (remove)" or "decision input (keep, say why)"); screenshots at 1280px and 390px, light and dark, runner owner and a new user without a runner; E2E through `tests/fixtures/local-harness.js` and `SELECTORS`; `ci-success` green.

## Landed (close-out, 3 Nov 2026)

Implemented as the approved plan's D7 (type): about four sizes through the existing token set, no phone shrink of body text, mono only for IDs and figures. PR [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2256](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2256>), squash-merged as `048c3319` (checked head `4ffdd2cf`, CI green); live on [harbour.cat](<http://harbour.cat>). Deviations from the plan: LIN-3987's first-screen fit was dropped by ruling `lin4107-change-sheet-first-screen` (option a); the copy-first line no longer names the step before the press (D3). This description had no embedded plan, research or scoping sections to prune (the sections above are the slice's scope and tests, kept). The full pre-close description is preserved in the task snapshots (latest `4b90f047-1648-44c8-af15-f8257804ca04`) and the story is in the comment trail. Outside follow-ups: LIN-4161, LIN-4162.

comments.body:
**Beat 1 of 4: grounding, landing order, START greps (no code edits yet). Branch `feat/lin-4107-type-four-sizes` off `origin/main` 300c811f.**

**Landing order: LIN-4107 lands first; LIN-4017 rebases on it.** Reason: LIN-4017 is in Backlog with no assignee, no branch and no open PR, so nothing is in flight to collide with. Its rebuild is meant to reproduce today's rendering, so a size pass that lands first gives its visual replay a fixed baseline. The reverse order would make this slice rewrite a freshly rebuilt sheet. Recommendation; say if you want 4017 first.

**Drift since 27ae64ad (grounding) to 300c811f:** slices 1 to 4 have landed: LIN-4103 (#2224), LIN-4104 run control (#2225), LIN-4115 halt banner (#2226), LIN-4113 Home desk (#2241), LIN-4114 Waiting on you (#2247), LIN-4106 task page (#2254). The approach holds. The type scope is unchanged. Slice 4 touched the task page, so re-measure there.

**Type inventory (START).**
- Tokens (`public/style.css`): `--font-size-sm: 0.85em`, `--font-size-base: 1em`, `--font-size-lg: 1.25em` (around lines 103-105). Families: `--font-structural` (JetBrains Mono) and `--font-content` (Inter) at lines 48-49. No xs token. Note: `em` tokens compound when nested, so new tokens should be in rem.
- The ticket's test fails today: the Home and task stylesheets (style, common-actions, stage-track, run-control, session, swipe, chat, task-chat, task-page) hold 48 distinct `font-size` values, counting `var()` refs and `inherit`. Literals run from 9px to 26px and 0.7rem to 1.5rem. The test allows four.
- Phone shrink (`max-width` rules that set font-size): `style.css` at 640, 480, 400 and 360px (e.g. lines 1360, 2108, 2786, 2881, 3181); `session.css:685` at 480px; `swipe.css:967` at 400px; `task-page.css:213` at 720px. Need checking per selector which apply to Home classes.
- Mono: 71 lines in these sheets set `--font-structural`. Session classes (`.sess-task`, `.sess-chip`, `.sess-tx-msg`, `.sess-ctx-body`, `.sess-cred-token`, and others), `.task-ident`, `.task-share-url`, `.opened-task-generated`. Which of these carry the ruling options, the \"N sessions\" line and session names is not confirmed yet; that is beat 2/3 work.

**START greps (the plan's three; full hit lists saved in the builder's scratchpad).**
- Grep 1 (estimate names): 117 hits. Top files: lib/task-page-loader.js (11), lib/render-task-page.js (4), plus tests.
- Grep 2 (run-control names): 315 hits. Top files: public/prompt-section.js (33), plus tests and docs.
- Grep 3 (badge): 17 hits. Files: public/common.js (7), public/observation.js (6), lib/components/navbar.js (3), public/app.js (1).
Classification by file is done. The line-by-line display (remove) vs decision input (keep) pass waits for beat 3's END compare, since most of these belong to slices 1 to 4 and are already reclassified there. Nothing here is a type decision.

**Proposed four sizes, mapped to the existing token set (one addition):**
- `--font-size-lg` (1.25em): the ruling question and page headings only.
- `--font-size-base` (1em): body, ruling options, session names, row titles. No phone drop.
- `--font-size-sm` (0.85em): secondary text and the count line.
- `--font-size-xs` (NEW, 0.75rem, added beside the existing three): fine print and chips only.
Mono (`--font-structural`) only on IDs and figures. Every literal in the Home and task sheets folds into one of these four. Out of scope but counted by the test: swipe.css's 22 to 26px display sizes, which Home loads and so must be mapped too.

Next: beat 2 starts after the greps and token list are reviewed.

**Beat 2 of 4: type change committed (b4a8c44c)**

**5. Fourth-token decision and pins**
- No `--font-size-xs` was added: `grep -rn font-size-xs public lib` returns nothing.
- The fourth value is `inherit` within the mapped rules. Basis: LIN-4040 plan, D7 (type): "about four font sizes through the existing token set (LIN-4015)", and the LIN-4107 description: "use about four font sizes, through the existing token set".

**Beat 3 addendum: rulings A, B, C, D**

Branch `feat/lin-4107-type-four-sizes`, not pushed, no PR. Commits: `71391156` (A: task-page sizes, guard), `ba0ee1ab` (B: copy-first), `eb53c2c1` (refreshed evidence). Earlier beat-3 commits are `21db7390`, `2bd491a4`, `b60db899`.

**A. Task page sizes: fixed (scoped), with a guard**
- Before: 8 computed sizes on the task page: 24, 20, 18.72, 17, 16, 13.6, 11.56, 11.05px.
- Causes, each found in the running app:
  - Em tokens nested in em parents compound: `.opened-task-change` and `.task-stage-run` (13.6 x 0.85 = 11.56), `.task-ref-state` (11.56), and `h1 .task-ident` (sm inside the 20px title = 17px).
  - `code` inside `.sess-v`: Chrome scales the generic monospace family to 13/16 of an inherited size (11.05px). The face is set with the size, so the scaling does not apply. The code here is an ID, so mono is correct.
  - Browser default heading sizes: `h3.section-header` (1.17em = 18.72px) and the markdown `h2` (1.5em = 24px).
- Fix, in `public/task-page.css` (loaded by the task page only, so Home and the shared tokens do not change): nested elements take `inherit` (their parent's computed size), and the two headings take `--font-size-lg`. No `--font-size-*` token meaning changed.
- Runtime, the new list (`runtime-sizes.json`): task page, 3 distinct computed sizes at both widths: 13.6px (40 elements), 16px (33), 20px (4, the title and the headings). Home: 3, unchanged (16, 13.6, title 24 or 19.2).
- Guard: `tests/e2e/lin-4107-type-sizes.spec.js`, through the harness and `SELECTORS`. Every element with its own text must compute to one of 13.6, 16 or 20px, at 1280 and 390, and the two lists must match. Red on the old code (2 of 3 failing: 11.05, 11.56, 17, 18.72, 24px), green after (3 of 3).

**B. Copy-first step: removed, by the plan's explicit sentence**
- D3 of LIN-4040's approved plan: "No step is named before the press anywhere, including the copy-first line (item 5): the prompt says which step it is for once written." That covers the copy-first line explicitly, so the change is made.
- What the copy-first line said before the press: "the first step for a task in Todo" (Backlog: "...in Backlog"). It now reads "Write the prompt for this task. The prompt says which step it is for."
- What does not change: the button's `data-prompt` (the template the press writes, `plan` or `scoping`), which is behaviour and not on screen; and the step name, shown only after the prompt is written, which D3 allows.
- Retargeted pins, old -> new (each is the same pin on the new wording):
  - `tests/unit/lin-3833-copy-first-view.test.js`, Todo and Backlog rows: `the first step for a task in Todo` and `... in Backlog` -> `Write the prompt for this task. The prompt says which step it is for.`
  - `tests/unit/lin-4010-home-opened-task.test.js`, Backlog step line: `opened-task-step">the first step for a task in Backlog<` -> `opened-task-step">Write the prompt for this task. The prompt says which step it is for.<`
  - `tests/e2e/prompts.spec.js`, Todo step line: `toContainText('the first step for a task in Todo')` -> `toContainText('Write the prompt for this task. The prompt says which step it is for.')`, and the test title's "names its step from its status: Plan" -> "names no step before the prompt is written; ✦ Write the prompt writes Plan".
- The pins sit in those three files, not in the LIN-4016 tests the ruling named. No LIN-4016 assertion pins the wording.
- Correction to my beat-3 report: I said the copy-first line showed "Plan" before the press. It showed the "first step ... in Todo" wording only; "Plan" appeared after a prompt was written. The wording still named the step by its place, so it changed.

**C. `prompt-section.js:318/325` ("Run <step>")**
- Classified **decision input (keep)**: the stage name comes from the server's offer, and the offer carries one only after a failed or cancelled stage. Not changed, per the ruling.

**D. Review notes for the PR**
- The "Waiting on you" task line shows LOCAL-3 in sans, not mono. Left as is.
- Four mono selectors kept with names that do not settle them: `.card-meta`, `.chat-fold`, `.sess-kv`, `.segment-bar__cell`.

**Screenshots, re-taken and looked at:** task page, owner light 390, owner dark 390, new user light 1280 (copy-first line now names no step). The 16 captures and the contact sheets are in `docs/reviews/_evidence-2026-11-03-lin4107/`; the task contact sheet is attached below.

## Survey spike 1a (implementation)

**1. Why it was difficult, and where it bound.**
Yes, it was difficult. The type scale lived nowhere. It was about 48 literal `font-size` values, mostly `em`, in nine stylesheets that every page shares.
- **Shared sheets.** `style.css` serves every page, and nothing mapped selectors to the pages that render them. I classified by grepping class names, and got the scope wrong twice (`.page-header`, `.section-header--ruled`).
- **`em` nesting.** A parent's change moved every child: the task page drew 11.05, 11.56 and 17px, and the Change sheet grew about 31%.
- **One global phone body shrink (13px).** The header, nav and Change-sheet layouts held only because of it.

Tests pinned the old shape:
- **Literal values:** LIN-4024 12px, LIN-4009 1.5rem, LIN-3991 0.85em, 0.84rem, the 1.1em ruled-header ratio.
- **Phone layouts:** LIN-2191/4009 header rows, LIN-3987 Use on the first screen.

Each conflict needed a ruling mid-build, three in all. The static unit witness could not see the runtime cascade. CI went red on three E2E shards after a green local subset, and finding the causes took a bisect.

**2. What I would have done first.**
Two cheap things, before any mapping:
- **A census on main:** computed sizes on every page at 320, 390 and 1280px, with each selector tagged by the pages that render it.
- **A pin inventory:** every test that asserts a literal `font-size` or a phone layout.

Optionally, one small consolidation: give the nav chrome its own phone size instead of inheriting `body`. That would have surfaced all three rulings on day one, avoided the red CI round, the bisect and the misclassifications, and saved roughly half of beats 2 to 4.

**3. What the ticket or plan got wrong.**
- **"Four sizes through the existing token set."** There are three tokens, all `em`, so they compound; "four" had to mean `inherit`.
- **The witness** counted values in sheets shared by every page, so it measured the site, not Home.
- **"No phone shrink"** was framed as Home body text. It is one global rule that shell chrome and LIN-3987 depend on, and the plan didn't name that conflict.
- **My own mistakes:** a wrong copy-first report, and a truncated classifier.
